title: Squirrel Away
summary: A cloud document-management app with AI-powered search, OCR text extraction, and real-time file processing — Google Drive-like, built full-stack in TypeScript.
outcome: Started as a technical evaluation project and grew into a production-grade DMS: direct-to-cloud uploads, a hybrid OCR + AI search pipeline, and a background job queue — all in a type-safe TypeScript monorepo.

children.text: Squirrel Away began as a technical evaluation project — and turned into something I actually like using. It's a full-stack, production-grade document management system with Google Drive-like functionality: nested folders, sharing, starring, trash recovery, and a search that reads
your documents via a hybrid OCR + AI pipeline. Everything is TypeScript, end to end, in a Turborepo monorepo.

Document management sounds simple until you hit the real requirements: uploads that don't choke the API server, search that finds text inside scanned PDFs and images, and long-running processing (OCR, format conversion) that can't block the request cycle. The goal was to build all of it to a production bar, not a demo bar.
Files stream directly between the browser and Cloudflare R2 using presigned URLs. The API only issues URLs and stores metadata, so upload bandwidth never bottlenecks the server.
Drizzle ORM gives end-to-end TypeScript safety with types inferred from the schema — no runtime shape mismatches between DB, API, and frontend.
OCR, PDF splitting, and image conversion run in Redis-backed background workers. The UI polls for real-time 0–100% progress instead of hanging on long jobs.

Fast text extraction from digital PDFs first, Tesseract.js fallback for scanned documents, and OpenAI Vision for the hardest cases — plus AI-generated descriptions that make uploaded images searchable by content.
File management: nested folders with breadcrumbs, soft delete + trash recovery, starring, recent files, grid/list toggle, fully responsive.
File-processing queue: PDF page splitting, image format conversion (PNG/JPEG/WebP), thumbnail generation, exponential-backoff retries with job prioritization.
Auth via NextAuth v5 (Google + GitHub OAuth).
A CSS-variable theming system with warm branded palette and light/dark mode.

Files:       POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /files, /files/search, /files/recent, /files/starred
Folders:     POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /folders, /folders/:id/breadcrumb
Processing:  POST /processing/files/:id/ocr | /split | /convert
Health:      GET /health (DB + Redis connectivity)

Full-stack proficiency (Next.js + NestJS in one TypeScript monorepo), cloud architecture (S3-compatible storage, Redis queues, PostgreSQL), practical AI integration with a local fallback, and production patterns — auth, soft deletes, job queues, error handling — with UI/UX polish on top.

title: Task Board Manager
summary: A kanban-style task board with drag-and-drop columns, priorities, and due dates — built to show Angular + Express full-stack range and containerized deployment.

children.text: Task Board Manager is a kanban-style task app — columns, cards, drag-and-drop, priorities, and due dates. I built it as a portfolio demo specifically to show a different half of my toolkit:
Angular on the frontend and Express on the backend
, deliberately contrasting the Next.js/NestJS stack behind
Standalone components, typed models/interfaces, routing, a service layer, and Angular CDK powering the drag-and-drop between columns.
A clean REST surface for task CRUD plus status moves and a reset-to-seed endpoint:

GET    /api/tasks           # list
POST   /api/tasks           # create
PUT    /api/tasks/:id       # update
DELETE /api/tasks/:id       # delete
PUT    /api/tasks/:id/move  # move to another status/column
POST   /api/tasks/reset     # reset to initial data
The repo ships with a Dockerfile, docker-compose, nginx config, and Kubernetes manifests — the app is containerized and deploys to Railway.
A custom SCSS design system, responsive layout, modal forms for task creation/editing, and priority + due-date support on cards.
Range. Squirrel Away proves depth in the React/Next ecosystem; this proves I'm equally comfortable in Angular and can stand up a containerized, deployable full-stack app end to end.

title: Pioneer District Website
summary: The public website for the Pioneer District of the Barbershop Harmony Society — designed and built solo, and now being re-platformed from Gatsby to a Next.js 15 + Sanity monorepo. Live in production since 2020.
timeline: 2020–present (v1 Gatsby live; v2 Next.js 15 in progress)
client: Pioneer District Association of Chapters (Barbershop Harmony Society)

children.text: Pioneer District of the Barbershop Harmony Society

A volunteer-run music organization needed a site non-technical board members could keep current — events, news, convention info, award and history archives — without touching code, while also handling real donations and growing its mailing list.

title: WagerVault
summary: A universal (iOS/Android/Web) mobile app for tracking gambling sessions, bankroll, and performance — with a personal-vs-global RTP engine, charted analytics, and year-end tax estimation. In active development.
role: Founder / mobile full-stack (product, design, app, backend)

global Return-to-Player (RTP); and estimates year-end federal taxes from handpays. Built as a universal app, it runs on iOS, Android, and web from one codebase.

title: MI-X Chorus
summary: A compact site for the MI-X barbershop chorus (Pioneer District) to help singers discover the group and join — Angular with GSAP animation.
client: MI-X Chorus (Pioneer District, Barbershop Harmony Society)

children.text: (pronounced "EM-eye-X"), a barbershop chorus in the Pioneer District. The whole job is one clear goal: help prospective singers find the chorus and take the step to join. No sprawling feature set — a clean, welcoming front door.

for smooth, personable motion, and styled in SCSS. A small build script generates the member image list at build time, so the roster stays easy to update without a heavy backend. A Sanity backend was scaffolded but ultimately not adopted — the frontend runs cleanly on its own, which keeps the site simple and cheap to host.
Right-sizing a project: shipping a tidy, animated, purpose-built site that does one job well, without over-engineering. Also a second data point (alongside
) for comfort in Angular, and a taste of animation work via GSAP.
